```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import wilcoxon, mannwhitneyu, kruskal
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
from scipy.stats import spearmanr, rankdata
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor
```

```{python}
mitocarta = pd.read_excel("Human.MitoCarta3.0.xls", sheet_name="A Human MitoCarta3.0")
mito_genes = set(mitocarta["Symbol"].dropna().unique())
data_filtered = pd.read_csv("data_filtered.csv", index_col=0)
genes_metadata = pd.read_csv("tcga_brca_gene_metadata.csv",index_col=0)
sample = pd.read_csv("sample.csv",index_col=0)
meta_sub = pd.read_csv("sample_metadata_with_subtype.csv",index_col=1)
data_paired = pd.read_csv("data_paired.csv",index_col=0)
sample_paired = pd.read_csv("sample_paired.csv",index_col=0)
```

```{python}
# Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols 
data_filtered["gene_symbol"] = data_filtered.index.map(genes_metadata["gene_name"])
data_filtered = data_filtered.dropna(subset=["gene_symbol"])
data_filtered = data_filtered.drop_duplicates(subset="gene_symbol", keep="first")
data_filtered = data_filtered.set_index("gene_symbol")
```


```{python}
#The reason is sequencing depth. A sample with 40 million reads will show more counts for every gene than one #with 20 million, even if the biology is identical. Dividing by the total puts all samples on the same footing, #so gene in one tumor can be compared with same gene in another.
cpm = data_paired.div(data_paired.sum(axis=0), axis=1) * 1e6
#RNA-seq values are heavily right-skewed: a few genes and samples have huge values. Taking the log makes the #distribution closer to symmetric, which the correlations, regressions and z-scores in your analysis assume.
log_expr = np.log2(cpm + 1) 

#Subset to MitoCarta genes actually present in data
mito_genes_present = [g for g in mito_genes if g in log_expr.index]
print(f"MitoCarta genes found in your dataset: {len(mito_genes_present)} "
      f"out of {len(mito_genes)}")
 
mito_expr = log_expr.loc[mito_genes_present]
```


```{python}
gene_means = mito_expr.mean(axis=1)
gene_stds = mito_expr.std(axis=1)
z_scores = mito_expr.sub(gene_means, axis=0).div(gene_stds, axis=0)
mito_score = z_scores.mean(axis=0)   # average across genes, per sample
mito_score.name = "mitochondrial_score"
 
print("\nMitochondrial score summary:")
print(mito_score.describe())
 
#mito_score.to_csv("mitochondrial_score_per_sample_paired.csv")
```

```{python}
type_col = "tcga.cgc_sample_sample_type"

df = pd.DataFrame({"score": mito_score,
                   "patient": sample_paired["patient"],
                   "type": sample_paired[type_col]})
wide = df.pivot(index="patient", columns="type", values="score")
diff = wide["Primary Tumor"] - wide["Solid Tissue Normal"]

print("Patients:", len(diff))
print("Median paired difference:", round(diff.median(), 3))
print("Patients with tumor > normal:", (diff > 0).sum(), "of", len(diff))
print("Wilcoxon signed-rank p =", wilcoxon(diff).pvalue)

# effect size: paired difference relative to its spread
print("Effect size (mean diff / SD of diff):", round(diff.mean() / diff.std(), 2))
```

```{python}
#extract patient id and convert index to string, Takeing the first 12 characters of each TCGA barcode
meta_sub["patient"] = meta_sub.index.astype(str).str[:12]

# Assign one PAM50 subtype per patient
sub_map = (meta_sub.dropna(subset=["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"])
                   .drop_duplicates("patient")
                   .set_index("patient")["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"])#Uses patient ID as the index and retrieves their PAM50 subtype.

# check the match with 112 paired patients
print("Patients with a label:", diff.index.isin(sub_map.index).sum(), "of", len(diff))

#Combine expression differences with subtypes
res = pd.DataFrame({"diff": diff, "subtype": diff.index.map(sub_map)})
out = res.groupby("subtype", dropna=False)["diff"].agg(
    median="median",#Median tumor-normal difference within each subtype
    n="count",
    frac_tumor_higher=lambda x: round((x > 0).mean(), 2),
)#Fraction of patients with positive diff (tumor expression higher than normal).
print(out)
```

#Checking specific genes
```{python}
type_col = "tcga.cgc_sample_sample_type"

# 1. Normalize from the paired counts
cpm = data_paired.div(data_paired.sum(axis=0), axis=1) * 1e6
log_cpm = np.log2(cpm + 1)

genes = ["PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH", "SHMT1", "MTHFD1",
         "SFXN1", "SFXN2", "SFXN3", "SHMT2", "MTHFD2", "MTHFD1L"]
genes = [g for g in genes if g in log_cpm.index]

expr = log_cpm.loc[genes].T                      # samples x genes, log2 CPM

# 2. Check: this must pass, otherwise stop
print("Max value in expr:", round(expr.values.max(), 1))   # expect roughly 10-16
assert expr.values.max() < 30, "still looks like counts"
```

```{python}
# 3. Paired differences per subtype
def gene_diffs(sub):
    pats = res.index[res["subtype"] == sub]
    t = expr[(sample_paired[type_col] == "Primary Tumor") &
             sample_paired["patient"].isin(pats)].copy()
    n = expr[(sample_paired[type_col] == "Solid Tissue Normal") &
             sample_paired["patient"].isin(pats)].copy()
    t.index = sample_paired.loc[t.index, "patient"] #Replaces sample IDs with patient IDs
    n.index = sample_paired.loc[n.index, "patient"]
    return t - n.loc[t.index]
#t - n calculates the difference in expression for every gene.
#n.loc[t.index] reorders normal samples to match the order of tumor samples.

gb, gl = gene_diffs("Basal"), gene_diffs("LumB")

#Calculate effect sizes and statistical significance
out = pd.DataFrame({
    "log2FC_Basal": gb.median(), "log2FC_LumB": gl.median(),
    "p_Basal": [wilcoxon(gb[g]).pvalue for g in genes],
    "p_LumB": [wilcoxon(gl[g]).pvalue for g in genes],
    "p_direct": [mannwhitneyu(gb[g], gl[g]).pvalue for g in genes],#We are comparing two independent groups of paired differences.
}, index=genes)
for c in ["p_Basal", "p_LumB", "p_direct"]:
    out["padj_" + c[2:]] = multipletests(out[c], method="fdr_bh")[1] 
#why  multipletests? We're testing many genes, not just one.
#For example, if you test 1,000 genes using a significance threshold of 0.05, some genes may appear significant just by chance.
#We use Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) to control the false discovery rate (FDR)


pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", None)
print(out[["log2FC_Basal", "padj_Basal", "log2FC_LumB", "padj_LumB", "padj_direct"]].round(3))
```

- **Cytosolic serine synthesis** (PHGDH, PSAT1) rises in Basal and not in LumB. 

- **Mitochondrial serine import** (SFXN1, SFXN2) rises mainly in LumB.


- SHMT2 and MTHFD2, the main mitochondrial one-carbon enzymes, rise in both subtypes (direct padj \~1.0), and MTHFD2 is the largest change in the table for both. So Basal tumors are not avoiding the mitochondrial route.

both subtypes activate one-carbon metabolism in the mitochondria, but they differ in how serine is supplied: Basal makes it in the cytosol (PHGDH/PSAT1), while LumB looks more dependent on importing it into mitochondria (SFXN1/2).


**check whether it replicates without the normals.** The paired analysis has only 17 Basal and 22 LumB patients. All 1,109 TCGA tumors include about 190 Basal-like, so compare the same genes across subtypes in tumors only:

```{python}
# log2 CPM from the full filtered counts
cpm_all = data_filtered.div(data_filtered.sum(axis=0), axis=1) * 1e6
logcpm_all = np.log2(cpm_all + 1)

# tumors only, with PAM50 (meta_sub from sample_metadata_with_subtype.csv, indexed by barcode)
meta_sub = meta_sub.set_index("tcga.tcga_barcode") if "tcga.tcga_barcode" in meta_sub.columns else meta_sub
tum = meta_sub[(meta_sub["tcga.cgc_sample_sample_type"] == "Primary Tumor") &
               meta_sub["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"].isin(["Basal", "Her2", "LumA", "LumB"])]
tum = tum[tum.index.isin(logcpm_all.columns)]
print(tum["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"].value_counts())

genes = ["PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH", "SFXN1", "SFXN2", "SFXN3", "SHMT2", "MTHFD2", "MTHFD1L"]
rows = []
for g in genes:
    v = logcpm_all.loc[g, tum.index]
    grp = {s: v[tum["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"] == s] for s in ["Basal", "Her2", "LumA", "LumB"]}
    rows.append({"gene": g,
                 **{f"median_{s}": grp[s].median() for s in grp},
                 "p_Basal_vs_LumB": mannwhitneyu(grp["Basal"], grp["LumB"]).pvalue,
                 "p_kruskal": kruskal(*grp.values()).pvalue})
t = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("gene").round(3)
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", None)
print(t)
```

Serine synthesis (PHGDH, PSAT1) and the SFXN1/SFXN2 shift are graded: Basal > Her2 > luminal. MTHFD1L is the exception. It is high only in Basal, with Her2 near luminal, so it is the most Basal-specific gene in the set. SHMT2 and MTHFD2 are about equal in Basal and Her2.
